## Part 1. Fonts: CSS or bslib?

I would use bslib, because it keeps the whole app consistent and is easier to change.

## Part 2. Three apps with R datasets

### mtcars

Number of cylinders and a maximum weight. The plot and the table show the same cars.Heavier cars use more fuel.

<iframe src="https://evandromsg.shinyapps.io/mtcars/" width="100%" height="800" style="border:none;"></iframe>

### USArrests

Type of crime and how many states to show. Same sorted list of states. Southern states lead in murder arrests. Nevada leads in rape arrests.

<iframe src="https://evandromsg.shinyapps.io/usarrests/" width="100%" height="700" style="border:none;"></iframe>

### uspop

Choose a range of census years. It is up to you using a log scale. The plot and the table use the same years. On the log scale the line is almost straight until 1860, which means the population grew at a nearly constant rate.

<iframe src="https://evandromsg.shinyapps.io/uspop/" width="100%" height="800" style="border:none;"></iframe>

## Part 4. My own app: hate crimes and inequality

This app uses FiveThirtyEight data on hate crimes reported to the FBI (2010-2015 average). The plot and the table use the same filter on how urban each state is. With the District of Columbia, the correlation between inequality and hate crimes is 0.42, but without DC it is close to zero (0.06), so one extreme case creates the pattern.

<iframe src="https://evandromsg.shinyapps.io/meu_app/" width="100%" height="900" style="border:none;"></iframe>
